items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: I mentioned it to Paul one time. It’s the best he ever played... I mentioned it to him one time and he just looked at me and smiled.

ctx.x: That’s really interesting. I want to go back to, you mentioned Paul Desmond, which surprises me a little bit.

Oh it surprises a million people. It even surprises me sometimes, but I’m constantly hearing that guy. I got to know him in his later years. I met him a few times when I was a kid but the thing that appealed to me was his simplicity. And I certainly don’t play simple © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

all the time. But there’s a certain lyrical simplicity that he has that makes me play a certain way. And not that he was the only guy — I mean, you know Miles certainly influenced me too. But Paul is a saxophone player, being the first — they say you never forget your first love, you know? Like a woman or whatever. It’s like I don’t forget my first influence.
